newsitem.title: ITALY: Talks on lira ERM return can start any time-Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Talks on lira ERM return can start any time-Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said talks on returning the lira to Europe's exchange rate mechanism can start at any time.
Prodi told a news conference in Rome: "With the approval of the budget in the lower house, I believe talks about re-entry of the lira to the ERM can start."
"We have already said that with the approval of the budget in the lower house we can start talks," he added.
The 1997 budget was passed by the lower house at the weekend.
"The premises for taking our currency back into the ERM are there," Prodi said.

He referred to measures outlined today on Italy's new Euro tax to propel the country into a position to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) saying, "With today's decisions we have taken the last step to really start decisive negotiations on this subject."
Pressed about when the lira would return, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi speaking at the same conference said no country would reveal its exact plans ahead of time.

The government has said the budget approval in the lower house was needed before it would try to put the lira back in the ERM, with Ciampi recently saying this might be at the end of November and Prodi seeing it before the end of the year.
The lira, which left the ERM in a currency crisis in September 1992, was unmoved by the comments, trading little changed from earlier at 1,006.60/6.90 per mark.
